newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks weak in morning,led by properties.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks weak in morning,led by properties.

text.p: Property counters led Hong Kong stocks lower in Tuesday morning trade, after overnight volatility on Wall Street prompted some caution among investors, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index was down 74.50 points at 13,443.06. Turnover was HK$2.03 billion after the first hour of trade.

"The market is getting a bit nervous," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities. "It is trying to find a trading range and consolidate a bit before the next upleg starts," he said.
Analysts said the market seemed to be taking a pause after a buying frenzy pushed the Hang Seng index to a record intra-day high at 13,744.30 last Thursday.
"Probably going into next week it will be more quiet," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
He saw the index trading 100 to 200 points either side of 13,500 this week.
Tsang said the Hong Kong stock exchange's inquiry into unusually volatile trading last Thursday had also affected market sentiment. "That affects the turnover for blue chip companies," he said.
Shares in properties companies led the decline with Cheung Kong down HK$1.00 at HK$68.50 and Henderson Land off HK$1.00 at HK$78.50.
New World Development fell HK$1.50 to HK$51.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties was down HK$0.75 at HK$96.25.

Shares of Shun Shing Holdings rose HK$0.215 to HK$0.53. The company said Cosco (H.K.) Property Development had agreed to buy a 30 percent stake in the company from Golden Success Ltd for HK$0.315 per share.
Cosco (H.K.) Property is a wholly owned unit of COSCO (Hong Kong) Group which is the holding company of COSCO Pacific.
Shares in COSCO Pacific rose HK$0.05 to HK$7.65.
HSBC Holdings was down HK$1.00 at HK$161.50 but Bank of East Asia rose HK$0.10 to HK$33.40.
Wheelock, which is due to release interim results on Wednesday, fell HK$0.30 to HK$22.00.
Analysts said they expected net profit of HK$800 million to HK$1.04 billion for the six months ended September 30 compared with net profit of HK$1.51 billion in the same year-ago period.
